question: Should consecutive malformed `pullAudio` payloads count toward the existing five-input-error bridge shutdown cutoff?
rationale: The validation itself is correct, but whether protocol-corrupt audio should terminate an active bridge after five failures is a user-visible availability policy that the existing implementation history does not explicitly settle.

options.title: Count malformed chunks
options.body: Treat malformed chunks like other input failures and close the bridge after five consecutive failures, bounding repeated corrupt input and matching the existing recovery model.

options.title: Drop without shutdown
options.body: Reject each malformed chunk but keep the bridge alive indefinitely, favoring availability while risking repeated warnings and a permanently unusable input stream.

options.title: Define a separate threshold
options.body: Introduce a distinct malformed-payload policy, which offers finer control but expands configuration or hard-coded policy beyond this focused fix.

recommendation.title: Count malformed chunks
recommendation.body: Treat malformed chunks like other input failures and close the bridge after five consecutive failures, bounding repeated corrupt input and matching the existing recovery model.
